script.text: I thought one thousand subscribers would unlock a different version of me. Same face. Less panic. Possibly better posture.
Before that number, every unfinished drawing had an excuse. I'm still starting. Once I get there, I'll know what I'm doing.
Then we reached it. I was so happy. I kept looking at the number like it might quietly change its mind.
The next morning, I opened my project. Same desk. Same unfinished frame. Same hand that looked like a tiny bunch of bananas.
Excuse me. Where was the update? I'd reached the checkpoint. Why was I still the tutorial character?
And now my brain had a new problem. Before, I was scared nobody would watch. Now, I was scared people would.
So I tried to make the next video worthy of a thousand people. I redrew one face until it somehow looked less human. Excellent progress.
I thought a milestone would make the work feel smaller. Actually, no. I'd just given my self doubt a larger audience.
But something did change. Those weren't just extra digits. People had found these little stories, watched them, and decided they wanted another one.
The number didn't finish my drawing. It didn't promise the next video would work. It meant I wasn't putting all this into an empty room anymore.
So I'm still here, at the same desk, making the next frame. The hand still needs help. Apparently, confidence wasn't included. But you were.
